messages:
ashley: kicking off staged deploy for routing-policy-v2 to prod-2 — canary at 5% traffic starting now. watch latency/5xx and policy-eval errors. if we see >2s p99 regression or >0.5% 5xx, we abort and pin to previous release. assigns: kevin on rollback, sam on metrics, maya on runbook ops :shipit:

deploy-bot: canary started for routing-policy-v2 on prod-2 · canary-id=c-1727 · targets=5% · start_ts=2670000000

kevin: copying runbook link — who's owner for the emergency backout steps? want the explicit pin command and DB-tolerance notes.

ashley: @kevin i'm owner for this rollout. backout runbook here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backout-routing-policy-v2 — TL;DR pinned-image + traffic-reroute + cache-warmdown. also see ops checklist snippet below:
```
1) stop canary: deployctl canary abort --id c-1727
2) pin service image: infractl pin --service-routing routing-service --image sha256:abcd1234
3) route 100% traffic to routing-service-v1 via traffic-gate
4) invalidate prefix cache: cachectl invalidate --prefix /route/policy
5) rollback feature flags: ffctl set routing-v2 false --env prod
6) verify 200 OK and latency within SLOs
```

sam: seeing a small uptick in policy-eval latency in canary logs (p50 +30ms, p99 +220ms). no 5xx yet. digging into GPU batching logs.

maya: i pulled the runbook into the incidents playbook index and added the contact card for the DB team. also added a post-backout verification checklist.

kevin: good — if we abort i will follow steps 1..4 and call for a quick hotfix if pin doesn't restore service. who will own the postmortem?

ashley: i'll own the postmortem and release notes updates. kevin, please prepare the exact commands for the rollback snippet so oncall has copy-paste friendly steps.

deploy-bot: canary metrics update · canary-id=c-1727 · elapsed=180s · p99_latency=2.2s · 5xx_rate=0.08% · signals: latency:rising :warning:

sam: p99 just spiked again to 2.5s at 2670000180. i'm toggling down batching config on the canary host to isolate. if that doesn't fall, we pull the abort.

oncall-bot: reminder: change window expires in 25 minutes. if abort occurs after window, please file emergency-change with approvals.

ashley: decision: hold 30s to see if batching tweak buys us time. if p99 >2.3s for two consecutive samples abort. kevin stand by to run pin.

kevin: ready. rollback snippet prepared below for copy/paste:
```
# abort canary and pin previous image
deployctl canary abort --id c-1727 && infractl pin --service-routing routing-service --image sha256:prev9876 && trafficctl set-route --service routing-service --to-version v1 --percent 100
# invalidate caches and clear KV
cachectl invalidate --prefix /route/policy && kvctl delete --prefix policy_temp
# quick smoke
curl -sfS https://prod-2.routing-service/health || echo "smoke failed"
```

sam: latency fell back to 1.9s after batching tweak. p99 stable for two samples. 5xx remains <0.1%. no abort. :relieved:

ashley: keeping canary running to 10 minutes then slow roll to 25% if stable. all owners keep eyes on dashboards. if anything else, call for abort immediately.

maya: i'll update the runbook with the rollback snippet and tag kevin as secondary owner. adding a note to preserve logs: `log-archive --range last-15m --tag routing-policy-v2`

kevin: noted. prepping a short release note blurb in case we need to communicate to customers: "We paused routing-policy-v2 canary due to elevated p99 latency; rolling back to v1 while we investigate."

deploy-bot: canary metrics update · canary-id=c-1727 · elapsed=600s · p99_latency=1.95s · 5xx_rate=0.03% · status=stable

ashley: thanks team. leaving this thread open until traffic reaches 25% or we abort. if we abort, follow the runbook steps and ping #incidents. :eyes:
